parts.title: Part 1

passage.title: Computers
passage.content:
A computer is a machine that helps people do many tasks. It can process data, run programs, and show information on a screen. Every _____ has parts like a keyboard, screen, and mouse. The _____ lets the user type words and numbers into the computer.

_____ use computers at home, in schools, and at work. A user can write documents, play games, or watch videos. Each program on the computer helps the user do something special. For example, one _____ may help with drawing, while another helps with math.

The _____ shows what the computer is doing. It displays data like pictures, text, and videos. When the user types on the keyboard, the computer takes that _____ and shows it on the screen.

In today's world, computers are important tools. They help us learn, work, and have fun.

questions.hint: Every _____ has parts like a keyboard
The _____ shows what the computer is doing

parts.instruction: Read the text. Fill in each gap with ONE word. You must use a word which is somewhere in the rest of the text.

q1.text: The passage is about computers. The sentence lists parts that belong to a computer, such as a keyboard, screen, and mouse. That's why the correct answer is 'computer'.
q1.quote: A computer is a machine that helps people do many tasks.

q2.text: The sentence describes the action of typing words and numbers. The keyboard is the part of a computer that is used for typing. That's why the correct answer is 'keyboard'.

q3.text: The first sentence of the passage says that computers are machines that help people. This sentence describes who uses computers in different locations. That's why the correct answer is 'people'.
q3.quote: A computer is a machine that helps people do many tasks.

q4.text: The previous sentence introduces the idea that programs help users do special things. This sentence gives examples of these special tasks, like drawing and math. That's why the correct answer is 'program'.
q4.quote: Each program on the computer helps the user do something special.

q5.text: The sentence describes the function of displaying what the computer is doing. The next sentence clarifies this by mentioning it displays pictures, text, and videos. That's why the correct answer is 'screen'.
q5.quote: It displays data like pictures, text, and videos.

q6.text: The passage states that a computer's job is to process data. When a user types, they are inputting information for the computer to process and display. That's why the correct answer is 'data'.
q6.quote: It can process data, run programs, and show information on a screen.

parts.title: Part 3

paragraphs.content: The English word 'cat' (Old English catt) is introduced to many languages of Europe from Latin cattus and Byzantine Greek katta, including Portuguese and Spanish gato, French chat, German Katze, Lithuanian kate and Old Church Slavonic kotka, among others. The ultimate source of the word is Afroasiatic, presumably from Late Egyptian caute, the feminine of caus 'wildcat'. The word was introduced, together with the domestic animal itself, to the Roman Republic by the first century BC.

The domesticated cat and its closest wild ancestor are both organisms that possess 38 chromosomes and roughly 20,000 genes. About 250 heritable genetic disorders have been identified in cats, many similar to human inborn errors. The high level of similarity allows many of these diseases to be diagnosed using genetic tests that were originally developed for use in humans.

Cats as well as humans can experience some illnesses. Cats can suffer from a wide range of health problems, including infectious diseases, parasites, injuries, and chronic disease. Vaccinations are available for many of these diseases, and domestic cats are regularly given treatments to eliminate parasites such as worms and fleas.

In addition to obvious dangers, cats may be poisoned by many chemicals usually considered safe by their human guardians, because their livers are less effective at some forms of detoxification than those of many other animals, including humans and dogs. Cats may be particularly sensitive to environmental pollutants. When a cat has a sudden or prolonged serious illness without any obvious cause, it has possibly been exposed to a toxin.

Domestic cats use many vocalizations for communication, including purring, trilling, hissing, growling or snarling, grunting, and several different forms of meowing. By contrast, feral cats are generally silent. Their types of body language, including position of ears and tail, relaxation of whole body, and kneading of paws, are all indicators of mood. The tail and ears are particularly important social signal mechanisms.

Among domestic cats, males are more likely to fight than females. Among feral cats, the most common reason for cat fighting is competition between two males. In such cases, most fights are won by the heavier male. Another common reason for fighting in domestic cats is the difficulty of establishing territories within a small home. Female cats also fight over territory or to defend their kittens.

parts.title: Part 4

passage.title: Jason
passage.content:
Jason sat up in bed and rubbed his eyes. It was unusually dark for 7 a.m., and his phone screen wouldn't turn on. He reached over to check the lamp on his bedside table, but it didn't work either. 'Power cut,' he thought, but something about the silence in the house felt wrong. Normally, he could hear the hum of the fridge or the sound of his neighbor's dog barking. But this morning, everything was still. Strangely still.

He pulled the curtain aside. The street outside looked exactly the same as always-except for one thing: it was completely empty. No early walkers. No delivery vans. Not even the usual cat that crossed his yard every morning. The houses around him looked dark, their curtains still drawn. He checked his watch-8:10. People should have been awake by now.

Jason pulled on a hoodie and jeans and went downstairs. As he passed the hallway mirror, he noticed something odd-his reflection looked slightly distorted, as if the glass was bending the image. He stared at it for a few seconds, then shook his head. 'Maybe I didn't sleep well,' he muttered.

The kitchen was no better. The fridge was silent, and when he turned the tap, no water came out. He picked up his phone again-still no signal. Not even emergency calls. That had never happened before. He tried turning on the radio, hoping to catch a news broadcast, but it only gave static. He felt a knot forming in his stomach.

He stepped outside. The air felt heavy, thick-like just before a thunderstorm. There were no sounds, not even birds. It was like the world had been placed on mute. He walked slowly toward the end of his street, passing familiar houses that now looked strangely unfamiliar.

Then he heard it. Footsteps behind him. Not rushed-calm, slow, steady. He turned sharply. No one. But just as he was about to convince himself it was nothing, he saw someone standing at the far corner. A tall figure in a long, dark coat. Not moving. Just... watching.

Jason froze. Something about the figure made him uneasy. He couldn't see their face-it was covered by a hood-but he could feel the stare. Then the figure slowly lifted a hand and waved.

He took a few steps backward, unsure whether to shout or run. Suddenly, a hand grabbed his shoulder from behind. He jumped and spun around, fists clenched.

It was Leo.

'Man, relax! It's just me,' Leo said, wide-eyed.

Jason let out a breath. 'You scared me to death. Where have you been?'

'I woke up like you. No power, no people. I tried calling you, but I couldn't get through. What's happening?'

Jason pointed toward the corner. 'Did you see that guy?'

Leo nodded. 'Yeah. I saw him earlier. He was standing outside my window.'

They both looked back at the corner. The figure was gone.

Suddenly, a loud, deep hum filled the air. It was like the sound of a distant engine, but it seemed to come from everywhere at once. The ground vibrated slightly beneath their feet.

Jason and Leo looked at each other.

'What if... this isn't just a blackout?' Jason whispered.

Leo's face was pale. 'Then we're not just dealing with a power cut.'

parts.title: Part 5

passage.title: Vertical Farming
passage.content:
As urban populations grow and arable land becomes increasingly limited, the demand for alternative methods of food production is higher than ever. Among these innovative approaches, vertical farming has gained significant attention. This method involves cultivating crops in vertically stacked layers, often within controlled indoor environments such as repurposed warehouses, skyscrapers, or specially designed containers. Unlike traditional agriculture, which relies heavily on sunlight, rainfall, and vast expanses of land, vertical farming utilizes LED lighting, climate control systems, and hydroponic or aeroponic techniques to grow food more efficiently and in less space.

The appeal of vertical farming lies largely in its resource efficiency. In conventional agriculture, vast amounts of water are required, much of which is lost through evaporation or poor irrigation methods. Vertical farms, however, use closed-loop irrigation systems that recycle water and nutrients, resulting in up to 95% less water usage. Moreover, because the growing environment is completely enclosed, crops are protected from pests and diseases, drastically reducing or even eliminating the need for chemical pesticides. This not only lowers environmental damage but also contributes to healthier produce.

Another key advantage of vertical farming is its potential to shorten supply chains. In many urban regions, fresh produce must travel hundreds or even thousands of kilometers before reaching consumers. This long-distance transportation not only increases food prices but also contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. Vertical farms can be located directly in cities-sometimes within supermarkets or on rooftops-allowing produce to be harvested and sold locally, often on the same day. This reduces spoilage, enhances freshness, and offers a more sustainable alternative to long-distance food distribution.

Despite its promise, vertical farming faces several technological and economic challenges. The cost of establishing a vertical farm can be prohibitive, particularly in areas where real estate prices are high. Specialized equipment, advanced climate control technologies, and energy consumption-especially from artificial lighting-can lead to high operational expenses. Although some farms have begun using solar panels or other renewable energy sources to reduce their carbon footprint, the reliance on electricity remains a major obstacle to scalability.

Additionally, vertical farming is currently limited in terms of the variety of crops it can support. Fast-growing, low-height crops such as lettuce, kale, spinach, and herbs thrive in vertical systems. However, crops like corn, wheat, rice, and fruit-bearing trees require much more space and energy to cultivate, making them unsuitable for vertical environments in their current form. As a result, vertical farming is best viewed as a supplement to traditional agriculture, rather than a full replacement.

Proponents of vertical farming argue that as technological innovations continue, costs will decrease, and efficiency will increase. Developments in automation, robotics, artificial intelligence, and renewable energy integration could help overcome many of the current limitations. For example, AI-driven monitoring systems can precisely control temperature, humidity, and nutrient levels, ensuring optimal growth conditions while reducing waste.

Critics, however, caution against overestimating the benefits of vertical farming without considering its energy dependence and limited crop diversity. They argue that placing such systems in densely populated areas may also compete with other urban development needs, such as housing and infrastructure. Furthermore, the ecological cost of producing artificial materials for building and maintaining vertical farms should not be overlooked when calculating their long-term sustainability.
